items.title: Fooled twice: People cannot detect deepfakes but think they can

judge.evidence_topic: Hyper-realistic manipulation of audio-visual content, i.e., deepfakes, presents a new challenge for establishing veracity of online content. Research on the human impact of deepfakes, addressing both behaviors in response to and cognitive processing of deepfakes, remains sparse.
judge.evidence_empirical: In a pre-registered behavioral experiment ( N = 210), we show that (a) people cannot reliably detect deepfakes
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimento comportamental) sobre a percepção humana de deepfakes, publicado em 2021, atendendo a todos os critérios. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: AI-synthesized faces are indistinguishable from real faces and more trustworthy

judge.evidence_topic: Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates that synthesis engines have passed through the uncanny valley and are capable of creating faces that are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.
judge.evidence_empirical: Our evaluation of the photorealism of AI-synthesized faces indicates that synthesis engines have passed through the uncanny valley and are capable of creating faces that are indistinguishable-and more trustworthy-than real faces.
judge.reason: O resumo confirma que o estudo realizou uma avaliação empírica do fotorealismo e da confiabilidade de rostos sintéticos, o que sustenta diretamente o achado principal de que são indistinguíveis e mais confiáveis que rostos reais. O método descrito é consistente com a natureza empírica do estudo mencionada no resumo.

items.title: AI Hyperrealism: Why AI Faces Are Perceived as More Real Than Human Ones

judge.evidence_topic: In Experiment 1 ( N = 124 adults), alongside our reanalysis of previously published data, we showed that White AI faces are judged as human more often than actual human faces—a phenomenon we term AI hyperrealism.
judge.evidence_empirical: In Experiment 1 ( N = 124 adults)... In Experiment 2 ( N = 610 adults), we used face-space theory and participant qualitative reports to identify key facial attributes that distinguish AI from human faces but were misinterpreted by participants
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico com participantes humanos que investiga a percepção de rostos sintéticos, estando dentro do escopo e do período solicitado. Os achados extraídos refletem precisamente o que foi relatado no resumo.

items.title: Real and Deepfake Face Recognition: An EEG Study on Cognitive and Emotive Implications

judge.evidence_topic: This study investigated healthy individuals' cognitive and emotional engagement in a visual discrimination task involving real and deepfake human faces expressing positive, negative, or neutral emotions.
judge.evidence_empirical: Electroencephalographic (EEG) data were collected from 23 healthy participants using a 21-channel dry-EEG headset; power spectrum and event-related potential (ERP) analyses were performed.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico com participantes humanos que investiga a percepção de rostos sintéticos (deepfakes), atendendo aos critérios. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e condizentes com o resumo.

items.title: Deepfake smiles matter less—the psychological and neural impact of presumed AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_topic: Here we investigate the impact of the belief that depicted persons are real or deepfakes on psychological and neural measures of human face perception.
judge.evidence_empirical: Using EEG, we tracked participants’ (N = 30) brain responses to real faces showing positive, neutral, and negative expressions, after being informed that they are either real or fake.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga a percepção humana sobre rostos presumidamente sintéticos (deepfakes), utilizando um método experimental com EEG e medidas comportamentais, o que se alinha ao pedido. O achado extraído é uma paráfrase direta e precisa do resumo.

items.title: Voice clones sound realistic but not (yet) hyperrealistic

judge.evidence_topic: We investigated the extent to which AI-generated voices sound real to human listeners, and whether listeners can accurately distinguish between human and AI-generated voices.
judge.evidence_empirical: We tested these questions using AI-generated voices generated with and without a specific human counterpart (i.e., voice clones, and voices generated from the latent space of a large voice model).
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico com participantes humanos sobre a percepção de vozes sintéticas, atendendo a todos os critérios. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e refletem fielmente o resumo.

items.title: Training human super-recognizers' detection and discrimination of AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_topic: Here, we investigate synthetic face detection and discrimination in super-recognizers (SRs; who have exceptional face recognition skills), and typical-ability control participants.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two different experimental designs, we found that SRs (total N = 283) were better at detecting and discriminating synthetic faces than controls (total N = 381)
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental com participantes humanos sobre a detecção de rostos sintéticos, alinhando-se perfeitamente ao pedido. O método e o achado extraídos estão corretamente representados no resumo.

items.title: What you see is not what you get anymore: a mixed-methods approach on human perception of AI-generated images

judge.evidence_topic: This study explores human perception and detection capabilities regarding AI-generated images of landscapes, architecture, and interiors using a mixed-methods approach.

items.title: Interpretation of AI-Generated vs. Human-Made Images

judge.evidence_topic: The goal of this study was to examine whether image interpretation is influenced by the origin of the image (AI-generated vs. human-made).
judge.evidence_empirical: To this end, we presented 24 AI-generated images (produced using Midjourney, DALL·E, and Firefly) and 8 human-made images to 161 participants
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico publicado em periódico em 2025 que investiga a percepção de credibilidade e realismo de imagens geradas por IA por participantes humanos, atendendo a todos os critérios. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Perception and social evaluation of cloned and recorded voices: Effects of familiarity and self-relevance

judge.evidence_topic: In the present study, we investigated whether listeners' perception and social evaluation of state-of-the-art voice clones depend on whether the clone being heard is a replica of the self, a friend, or a total stranger.
judge.evidence_empirical: Forty-seven of these experimental participants (and 47 unfamiliar controls) rated the Trustworthiness, Attractiveness, Competence, and Dominance of cloned and recorded samples of their own voice and their friend's voice.

items.title: Specific media literacy tips improve AI-generated visual misinformation discernment
